full_judgment: 2. The petitioner admittedly purchased the property from one Sushil Kumar Gangali by a kabala executed and registered at Badarganj Sub-Registry office in the district of Rangpur in 1975. The said Sushil Kumar Gangali had purchased the said property by a kabala executed and. registered at Calcutta in undivided British India in 1945. It is alleged that the said Sushil Kumar. Gangali was although a national and citizen of Pakistan and subsequently of Bangladesh and having always resided in East Pakistan and Bangladesh never migrated to India nor acquired the nationality and citizenship of India, only during the war of independence for nine months the said Sushil Kumar Gangali was away from in this country. In the affidavit-in-opposition by the Custodian of the vested property nothing has been alleged that the said Sushil Kumar Gangali ever acquired Indian nationality or that he, permanently resided in India and thereby became enemy national between September, 1965 and December, 1971. In this connection it may be mentioned that a kabala executed and registered in Bangladesh in 1975 creates a presumption that the registration authority satisfied that the executants was a valid citizen and national of Bangladesh since an Indian national as such could not transfer any property in Bangladesh by way of any registered deed. Mr. Anwarul Huq Chowdhury, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the Government and Custodian of vested property has pointed out that notwithstanding the aforesaid kabalas the names of the petitioner and his immediate predecessor in interest Sushil Kumar Gangali do not appear in the records of rights. The records of rights of the Government which at best are evidence of possession at the time when such records are prepared and not an evidence of title as such. This is a well established principle of law. A registered kabala is an evidence of title which will prevail over the other records of rights as such until and unless such kabala is cancelled on a specific allegation of fraud by any civil court in an appropriate civil suit.
